source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Basis criterion
statement: A collection B of subsets of S is a basis for a topology iff it covers S and every point of B1 intersection B2 lies in a basis element contained in that intersection.
conditions: B is a collection of subsets of S.
conclusion: Unions of basis elements form a topology on S.
common_misuses: Checking only that basis elements cover S.
bridge_lemmas: Finite intersections can be refined pointwise.
repair_templates: Verify both covering and intersection-refinement conditions.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Compact subsets of Hausdorff spaces are closed
statement: Every compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed.
conditions: S is Hausdorff.
K is compact in S.
typical_uses: Prove compact manifolds are closed in ambient Hausdorff spaces.
bridge_lemmas: Open-cover compactness yields a finite subcover separating a point from K.
repair_templates: State Hausdorffness explicitly before invoking closedness.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Compact-to-Hausdorff continuous bijection
statement: A continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.
conditions: f:X->Y is continuous and bijective.
X is compact and Y is Hausdorff.
typical_uses: Identify quotient constructions with familiar compact manifolds.
common_misuses: Assuming a continuous bijection is always a homeomorphism.
bridge_lemmas: Closed subsets of compact spaces are compact.
repair_templates: Prove compactness of the source and Hausdorffness of the target.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Tangent vector as a derivation
statement: A tangent vector at p is a linear map v:C-infinity_p(M)->R satisfying v(fg)=v(f)g(p)+f(p)v(g).
conditions: M is a smooth manifold and p is in M.
conclusion: T_pM is a vector space of point derivations at p.
typical_uses: Define tangent spaces independently of coordinates.
common_misuses: Treating a derivation as an ordinary global vector field.
bridge_lemmas: Taylor expansion identifies derivations with coordinate directional derivatives.
repair_templates: Specify the base point and Leibniz rule.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Chain rule for manifold differentials
statement: For smooth maps f:M->N and g:N->P, d(g composition f)_p equals dg_{f(p)} composition df_p.
conditions: f and g are smooth.
typical_uses: Compute tangent maps and prove rank identities.
repair_templates: Track the base point f(p) in the middle differential.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Constant rank theorem
statement: A smooth map of constant rank r is locally equivalent in suitable charts to the projection (x1,...,xn)->(x1,...,xr,0,...,0).
conditions: f:M^m->N^n is smooth and has rank r on a neighborhood of p.
conclusion: Local coordinates put f into projection normal form.
typical_uses: Derive immersion, submersion, and level-set normal forms.
common_misuses: Applying the theorem at an isolated point without constant rank nearby.
bridge_lemmas: Inverse function theorem and matrix rank theorem.
repair_templates: Establish rank constancy on a neighborhood before choosing adapted charts.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Regular level set theorem
statement: If c is a regular value of a smooth map f:M->N, then f^{-1}(c) is an embedded submanifold of codimension dim N.
conditions: df has full rank dim N at every point of f^{-1}(c).
conclusion: The level set is a smooth manifold with tangent space ker df.
common_misuses: Checking regularity only at one point.
repair_templates: Verify surjectivity of df along the entire level set.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Submersions are open maps
statement: A smooth submersion is locally a projection and therefore maps open sets to open sets.
conditions: f:M->N is a smooth submersion.
conclusion: f is an open map and has local smooth sections.
common_misuses: Confusing submersion with an arbitrary surjective map.
repair_templates: Use local projection coordinates to prove openness.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Local flow existence and uniqueness
statement: A smooth vector field determines a unique maximal integral curve through each initial point, with smooth dependence on initial data where defined.
conditions: X is a smooth vector field on M.
conclusion: Integral curves form a local flow; completeness gives a global flow.
typical_uses: Define Lie derivatives and group actions.
common_misuses: Assuming every vector field is complete.
bridge_lemmas: Local ODE existence and uniqueness in charts.
repair_templates: Restrict the time interval or prove completeness separately.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Lie bracket characterizes commuting flows
statement: The Lie bracket [X,Y] vanishes iff the local flows of X and Y commute wherever both compositions are defined.
conditions: X and Y are smooth vector fields.
conclusion: Vanishing bracket is equivalent to local flow commutation.
common_misuses: Ignoring domains where both flows exist.
repair_templates: State the common flow domain explicitly.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Cartan homotopy formula
statement: For a vector field X, Lie derivative on forms satisfies L_X = i_X d + d i_X.
conditions: X is smooth and the operators act on differential forms.
conclusion: Lie derivative decomposes into contraction followed by exterior derivative and vice versa.
typical_uses: Prove invariance and derive identities for forms.
common_misuses: Using i_X d alone and omitting d i_X.
repair_templates: Check form degrees and operator signs.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Poincare lemma
statement: Every closed differential form on a star-shaped open subset of Rn is exact in positive degree.
conditions: U is star-shaped and omega is a closed k-form with k>0.
conclusion: There exists eta with d eta = omega.
common_misuses: Applying it globally on noncontractible manifolds.
repair_templates: Restrict to a contractible chart or use a global cohomology argument.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Stokes theorem
statement: For an oriented compact smooth n-manifold with boundary and a compactly supported (n-1)-form omega, integral over M of d omega equals integral over boundary M of omega with induced orientation.
conditions: M is oriented, compact, smooth, and has boundary.
omega is a smooth (n-1)-form.
conclusion: Integral of an exterior derivative is a boundary integral.
typical_uses: Derive Green and fundamental theorem identities.
common_misuses: Forgetting boundary orientation or compact support.
bridge_lemmas: Local coordinate change-of-variables and partition of unity.
repair_templates: State orientation and induced boundary convention.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Smooth partition of unity method
statement: A locally finite smooth partition of unity subordinate to an open cover allows local smooth data to be glued into a global object.
conditions: M is a smooth manifold and the cover is open (with compactness or countability hypotheses as needed).
conclusion: Local constructions can be summed smoothly because only finitely many terms are nonzero near each point.
typical_uses: Construct metrics, forms, extensions, and global sections.
repair_templates: Refine the cover and invoke local finiteness before summing.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Homotopy invariance of de Rham cohomology
statement: Smoothly homotopic maps induce the same map on de Rham cohomology; homotopy equivalences induce isomorphic cohomology.
conditions: f0,f1:M->N are smoothly homotopic.
conclusion: f0* = f1* on de Rham cohomology.
common_misuses: Assuming arbitrary continuous homotopies suffice without a smoothing argument.
bridge_lemmas: Cochain homotopy identity from integration over M x R.
repair_templates: Provide a smooth homotopy or invoke a smoothing theorem.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence
statement: An open cover M=U union V yields a long exact sequence in de Rham cohomology involving restriction maps and the connecting homomorphism.
conditions: U and V are open subsets covering M.
conclusion: Cohomology of M is related exactingly to that of U, V, and U intersection V.
typical_uses: Compute cohomology of unions and surfaces.
common_misuses: Using arbitrary subsets instead of open sets.
bridge_lemmas: Short exact sequence of de Rham complexes and partition of unity.
repair_templates: Choose an open cover and verify exactness at the cochain level.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Vector bundle local trivialization
statement: A rank-r vector bundle is locally diffeomorphic over each base open set U to U times Rr, with transition maps linear on fibers.
conditions: pi:E->M is a smooth bundle projection.
conclusion: Each fiber is an r-dimensional vector space and local frames exist.
typical_uses: Define tangent, cotangent, and tensor bundles.
common_misuses: Treating a locally trivial bundle as globally a product.
bridge_lemmas: Transition functions satisfy the cocycle condition.
repair_templates: Specify base projection and fiber-preserving trivializations.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Boundary orientation convention
statement: The orientation on the boundary of an oriented manifold is defined so that an outward-pointing normal followed by an oriented boundary basis gives the interior orientation.
conditions: M is an oriented smooth manifold with boundary.
conclusion: Boundary integration has a canonical induced orientation.
typical_uses: Apply Stokes theorem with correct signs.
common_misuses: Using inward normal or reversing the order.

source: Tu, An Introduction to Manifolds.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Quaternionic inner product
statement: For right quaternionic vectors x,y, define <x,y> = sum conjugate(x_i)y_i; it is conjugate-linear in the first argument and right-linear in the second.
conditions: x,y belong to H^n with right scalar multiplication.
conclusion: The form is positive definite and has norm squared <x,x>.
typical_uses: Define symplectic groups and quaternionic unitary maps.
common_misuses: Conjugating the wrong argument under right scalar conventions.
repair_templates: Fix left/right scalar convention before manipulating inner products.
